aboutH2: Canadian Therapy: outpatient and online counselling in Toronto
intro: Canadian Therapy is a private psychotherapy practice based in Toronto. It is not a residential rehab. There are no beds, no detox and no live-in program. Clients book 50-minute sessions with a Registered Psychotherapist or Registered Social Worker, and most of those sessions happen online by secure video, which means anyone in Ontario can use the service.

The practice was founded by Preeti Taneja, a Registered Social Worker who still sees clients as lead therapist. She set it up for people who want a therapist who understands their culture, and South Asian, immigrant and BIPOC clients make up a large part of the people it serves. Between them, the therapists speak English, Hindi, Punjabi, Urdu, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Farsi and French.

pillars.title: Talk therapy for drinking and drug use
pillars.body: Canadian Therapy lists addiction, alcohol abuse and codependency among the problems it works with. Three of its therapists, Shannon Kane, Miranda Elise Klimowski and Avista Amuyan, name addiction as a focus on the team page. Their methods include cognitive behavioural therapy, dialectical behaviour therapy, acceptance and commitment therapy, internal family systems and solution-focused brief therapy. This is weekly or regular counselling, so it suits someone who is safe to stay at home while they work on their use. Anyone who needs supervised withdrawal should arrange detox first and can use sessions here alongside or after it.

pillars.title: Therapists who understand where you come from
pillars.body: Founder Preeti Taneja built the practice for people who did not want to explain their culture before they could talk about their pain. Many of the therapists are South Asian, and sessions are offered in Hindi, Punjabi, Urdu, Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam as well as English, Farsi and French. The work often touches family expectations, immigration stress, intergenerational trauma and the shame some families attach to therapy. Couples sessions and 90-minute family sessions mean a partner or parent can join when substance use is affecting the whole household.

pillars.title: Online across Ontario, in person in Toronto
pillars.body: Most clients never visit an office. Sessions run by secure video, so someone in Brampton, Scarborough, Hamilton or Ottawa gets the same therapists as someone downtown. For people who prefer to meet face to face, Preeti Taneja, Taran Ranu and Lavanya Verma see clients in Toronto for an extra $30 per session. The practice's business address is in the Starwood Centre at 477 Richmond Street West, and its in-person booking page lists 692 Euclid Avenue near Bloor Street West.

overview: Substance use is one area of the work rather than the whole of it. The practice lists addiction, alcohol abuse and codependency among its services, and several therapists on the team name addiction as a focus, using approaches such as cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT), acceptance and commitment therapy and internal family systems. The same team also works with anxiety, depression, trauma, grief, burnout, ADHD and family conflict, which helps when drinking or drug use is tangled up with something else.

Couples and family sessions are available too. A couples session runs 55 minutes, and an extended relationship session of 90 minutes lets two or more people meet together. For people whose drinking or drug use is straining a marriage or a parent relationship, that can be a practical place to start.

location.heading: Canadian Therapy in Toronto, Ontario
location.intro: Canadian Therapy's business address is the Starwood Centre at 477 Richmond Street West in the King-Spadina area of downtown Toronto, and in-person bookings list an office at 692 Euclid Avenue, just north of Bloor Street West. Because most sessions are online, distance rarely matters, but for an in-person visit Mississauga is about 30 minutes by car, Scarborough and Markham about 35 to 40 minutes, Brampton about 45 minutes and Hamilton about an hour.

faqIntro: Answers come from Canadian Therapy's own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Canadian Therapy a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. Canadian Therapy is an outpatient psychotherapy practice, and most sessions take place online. It has no beds, detox or overnight program. You book individual, couples or family sessions and continue your normal life between them.

faqs.q: Does Canadian Therapy help with addiction and alcohol use?
faqs.a: Yes. The practice lists addiction, alcohol abuse and codependency among its services, and therapists Shannon Kane, Miranda Elise Klimowski and Avista Amuyan name addiction as a focus. Care is talk therapy, using methods such as CBT, DBT and acceptance and commitment therapy. Medical detox and medication are not offered.

faqs.q: How much does a session cost?
faqs.a: Individual sessions of 50 minutes cost between $165 and $280 including HST, depending on the therapist, and the first intake assessment starts at $185. Couples sessions start at $225 for 55 minutes, and a 90-minute extended relationship session is $325. In-person sessions add $30. The 20-minute first consultation is free.

faqs.q: Can I use my insurance or workplace benefits?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Many extended health plans in Ontario cover sessions with Registered Psychotherapists and Registered Social Workers, and the practice gives you a receipt after each session to submit yourself. It does not bill insurers directly, so check your plan's coverage before you start.

faqs.q: Is therapy online or in person?
faqs.a: Mostly online. Sessions run by secure video for clients anywhere in Ontario, including Toronto, Scarborough, Brampton, Mississauga and Ottawa. In-person sessions in Toronto are available with Preeti Taneja, Taran Ranu or Lavanya Verma for an extra $30 per session.

The business address is 477 Richmond Street West, Toronto (M5V 3E7), in the King-Spadina area of downtown. In-person bookings list an office at 692 Euclid Avenue, Toronto (M6G 2T9), north of Bloor Street West. Confirm which location your appointment is at when you book.

There is no fixed program length. Individual sessions are 50 minutes, couples sessions 55 minutes and family sessions 90 minutes, and you book them one at a time. Couples usually meet weekly or every two weeks, and some notice change in a few sessions while others stay longer.

No. You can book a free 20-minute phone consultation yourself online or by calling 647-559-0149, and the team will match you with a therapist or let you choose one. Doctors, clinics and agencies can also send a referral through the form on the practice's website.
No. Psychotherapists and social workers cannot prescribe. If medication might help, Canadian Therapy says it can refer you to a mental health physician who can assess you and prescribe if needed.

faqs.q: Is there culturally specific support for South Asian clients?
faqs.a: Yes, this is a main focus of the practice. Many of its therapists are South Asian, and they offer sessions in Hindi, Punjabi, Urdu, Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam as well as English. They work with family expectations, immigration stress and shame around asking for help, which can all affect substance use.
The practice's FAQ page asks for 24 hours' notice to cancel or move a session, or you may be charged. You can cancel online or by phone or email to your therapist.
